questions.stem: The G20 (Group of Twenty) PRESIDENCY was held by INDIA in:
questions.explanation: G20 (GROUP of TWENTY) — FORUM of 20 MAJOR ECONOMIES — 19 countries + European Union + (since 2023) African Union. Founded 1999 (FINANCE MINISTERS) after Asian Financial Crisis 1997. Elevated to LEADERS SUMMIT level in 2008 (post-Global Financial Crisis). MEMBERS (19 nations): Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, South Korea, Turkey, UK, USA + EU. Represents ~85% of global GDP, 75% of trade, 2/3 of world population. Presidency ROTATES annually. INDIA's PRESIDENCY (1 DEC 2022 – 30 NOV 2023): THEME 'VASUDHAIVA KUTUMBAKAM' ('The World is One Family') from Maha Upanishad; subtitle 'ONE EARTH, ONE FAMILY, ONE FUTURE'. LOGO: LOTUS + Earth. KEY PRIORITIES: (1) Green Development + climate finance + LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment). (2) Accelerated, Inclusive + Resilient Growth. (3) SDG Acceleration. (4) Technological Transformation + Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) — India's UPI + Aadhaar model showcased. (5) Multilateral Institutions Reform — push for UN + UNSC reform. (6) Women-Led Development. G20 SUMMIT in NEW DELHI, 9-10 SEPTEMBER 2023 — at BHARAT MANDAPAM (Pragati Maidan). Heads of State + Governments attended (except Xi Jinping + Putin who skipped — sent premiers). KEY OUTCOMES: (1) NEW DELHI LEADERS' DECLARATION — UNANIMOUS consensus (rare feat given Russia-Ukraine + US-China tensions; called diplomatic 'COUP' for Indian Sherpa AMITABH KANT). (2) AFRICAN UNION admitted as PERMANENT MEMBER — 21st member; India pushed strongly. G20 now informally 'G21'. (3) INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-EUROPE ECONOMIC CORRIDOR (IMEC) — announced; rail + shipping route India → UAE → Saudi → Israel → EU; counter to China's BRI. (4) Global Biofuels Alliance launched. (5) Digital Public Infrastructure framework + Aadhaar-UPI-ONDC promoted. (6) Finance Track — MDB reform, crypto regulation, debt restructuring. (7) Climate — tripling renewables by 2030. (8) ACCEPTANCE of India's Sherpa leadership; India chaired ~200 meetings in 60 cities. (9) Gandhi at Rajghat tribute by leaders. (10) CULTURAL showcase — kala + food + yoga. BRAZIL 2024 Presidency: theme 'Building a Just World + Sustainable Planet'. Rio summit Nov 2024. SOUTH AFRICA 2025 (current). USA 2026 (Trump's return affects vibe). G20 SUMMITS: (1) 2008 Washington (first, crisis response); (2) 2009 London + Pittsburgh; (3) 2010 Toronto + Seoul; ... (14) 2019 Osaka Japan; (15) 2020 Riyadh (virtual COVID); (16) 2021 Rome; (17) 2022 Bali; (18) 2023 DELHI; (19) 2024 Rio; (20) 2025 Johannesburg; (21) 2026 Miami. ASSOCIATED G20 TRACKS: SHERPA TRACK (political, social, economic) + FINANCE TRACK + Engagement Groups (B20 Business, C20 Civil, L20 Labour, S20 Science, T20 Think-Tanks, W20 Women, Y20 Youth, U20 Urban, P20 Parliaments). OTHER GROUPINGS: G7 (Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK, USA; since 1975; democratic advanced; most Fridays as 'G7+1 Russia' until 2014 Crimea). G77 (developing countries, ~134 members). NAM (Non-Aligned Movement) — 120+ members; Cold War origin. BRICS — Brazil, Russia, India, China, S Africa; expanded 2024 to BRICS+ adding Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi, UAE (5 new). SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation — China-led). QUAD (US, Japan, India, Australia). I2U2 (India, Israel, UAE, USA). IBSA (India, Brazil, S Africa). IORA (Indian Ocean Rim). 30 Nov 2023 — theme 'VASUDHAIVA KUTUMBAKAM' / 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'; SUMMIT held in New Delhi 9-10 Sept 2023; AU added as permanent member.

questions.stem: The SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) was founded in:
questions.explanation: SAARC (SOUTH ASIAN ASSOCIATION FOR REGIONAL COOPERATION) — regional intergovernmental organisation of 8 South Asian countries. FOUNDED: 8 DECEMBER 1985 at the 1st SAARC Summit in DHAKA, Bangladesh. 8 DECEMBER = SAARC Charter Day. Idea proposed by BANGLADESH's President ZIAUR RAHMAN in 1980. 7 FOUNDING members: BANGLADESH, BHUTAN, INDIA, MALDIVES, NEPAL, PAKISTAN, SRI LANKA. AFGHANISTAN joined APRIL 2007 as 8th member (at 14th SAARC Summit New Delhi). HQ: KATHMANDU (Nepal). COVERS: 3% of world's area + 21% of world's population (~2 billion people) + only 4% of world's GDP — demonstrates under-integration. OBJECTIVES (Charter): (1) Promote welfare + economic growth + social progress + cultural development in region. (2) Strengthen collective self-reliance. (3) Promote + strengthen mutual trust, understanding + appreciation of one another's problems. (4) Contribute to mutual trust + cooperative aims. STRUCTURE: (a) SUMMITS — annually supposed, but INFREQUENT due to India-Pakistan tensions. (b) COUNCIL OF MINISTERS. (c) STANDING COMMITTEES. (d) TECHNICAL Committees. (e) SECRETARIAT at Kathmandu headed by SECRETARY-GENERAL (3-year term, rotated). SAARC SUMMITS HELD: 1st Dhaka 1985 → 18th KATHMANDU 2014. Subsequent 19th summit planned for ISLAMABAD 2016 — CANCELLED after URI TERROR ATTACK (Sept 2016; India + 3 others boycotted citing Pakistani terror). SAARC in HIBERNATION since — NO SUMMIT for 10 years (as of 2024-25). INDIA + Pakistan rivalry major roadblock. KEY AGREEMENTS: (1) SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA, 1993) + SAARC Free Trade Area (SAFTA, 2006, in force Jan 2006). Tariff reduction phased. (2) SAARC FOOD BANK 2007 for food security. (3) SAARC Development Fund (SDF) 2010 — Thimphu. (4) SAARC Framework Agreement for Energy Cooperation 2014. (5) SAARC Convention on Narcotic Drugs (1990) + Suppression of Terrorism (1987). ACHIEVEMENTS LIMITED: only ~5-7% intra-regional trade (vs ASEAN 25%, EU 60%); low connectivity; low FDI between member countries. CHALLENGES: (1) India-Pakistan conflict overshadowing everything. (2) Low priority from Pakistan for SAARC. (3) Smaller neighbours (Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh) sometimes feel Indian dominance concern. (4) Bhutan + Bangladesh + Nepal + Sri Lanka (BBIN) sub-regional cooperation rising as alternative. (5) China's BRI + CPEC expanding. BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical + Economic Cooperation) — formed 1997; 7 members: India + Bangladesh + Bhutan + Myanmar + Nepal + Sri Lanka + Thailand; Pakistan + Afghanistan + Maldives NOT in it. Seen as potential SAARC alternative bypassing Pakistan. BIMSTEC Summit 2022 Colombo. BBIN (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal) — 2015 onwards; motor vehicles agreement (Bhutan's parliament still not ratified). INDIA's 'NEIGHBOURHOOD FIRST' POLICY (2014) — prioritises South Asian ties but bypasses Pakistan. Modi's inauguration 2014 + 2019 attended by SAARC leaders (except Pakistan in 2019 due to tensions). INDIA'S regional aid: (a) Neighbourhood Development Partnership Grant. (b) Vaccine Maitri (COVID vaccines to SAARC + world). (c) Pipelines (India-Nepal MOTIHARI-AMLEKHGANJ 2019), rail links, development aid. (d) LOCs (lines of credit) to Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Maldives, Bhutan. 7 founding members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka); Afghanistan joined 2007 (8 members); HQ Kathmandu.

questions.stem: BRICS was EXPANDED on 1 January 2024 with 5 NEW MEMBERS. The expanded 'BRICS+' now comprises:
questions.explanation: BRICS — major grouping of emerging economies. FOUNDING 4 (BRIC): BRAZIL + RUSSIA + INDIA + CHINA. Term coined 2001 by Jim O'Neill of GOLDMAN SACHS in paper 'Building Better Global Economic BRICs'. Formal cooperation begun 2006 (UN-level meeting) + first full summit 2009 YEKATERINBURG Russia. SOUTH AFRICA joined 2010 — making BRICS (5 members). EXPANSION — BRICS+ announced at 15th SUMMIT JOHANNESBURG SOUTH AFRICA (22-24 Aug 2023): invited 6 new members — EGYPT, ETHIOPIA, IRAN, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, SAUDI ARABIA, ARGENTINA. From 1 JANUARY 2024 they formally joined EXCEPT Argentina (new President Javier Milei, elected Dec 2023, rejected invitation — pro-Western pivot). Saudi Arabia status somewhat pending (slow movement). So BRICS+ = ORIGINAL 5 + 4-5 NEW = ~10 MEMBERS. REPRESENTS: ~45% of world population; ~35% of global GDP (PPP); ~25% nominal; major share of global reserves + oil + grain. OBJECTIVES: (1) Political dialogue + cooperation. (2) Economic + trade ties. (3) Alternative to Western-dominated IMF + World Bank + G7. (4) Multi-polar world order. (5) Financial autonomy from USD / SWIFT. KEY INSTITUTIONS (not equivalent to UN but emerging): (1) NEW DEVELOPMENT BANK (NDB) — est. 2014 SHANGHAI Summit; HQ SHANGHAI (CHINA). Offers loans for infrastructure + sustainability in BRICS + developing countries; alternative to World Bank. India's KV KAMATH was 1st President 2015-20. (2) CONTINGENT RESERVE ARRANGEMENT (CRA) — $100 BILLION currency swap fund for BRICS + EMs facing BoP crises; counter to IMF. Also BRICS PAY + BRICS Stock Exchange Forum + BRICS University League. SUMMITS: (1) 1st 2009 Yekaterinburg; (2) 2010 Brasília; (3) 2011 Sanya China; (4) 2012 New Delhi India; (5) 2013 Durban; (6) 2014 Fortaleza Brazil; (7) 2015 Ufa Russia; (8) 2016 GOA India; (9) 2017 Xiamen China; (10) 2018 Joburg; (11) 2019 Brasília; (12) 2020 virtual (COVID); (13) 2021 virtual India chair; (14) 2022 Beijing virtual; (15) 2023 JOBURG (expansion announced); (16) 2024 KAZAN RUSSIA (Putin's first major summit post-Ukraine invasion); (17) 2025 RIO BRAZIL; (18) 2026 India chair. KAZAN SUMMIT (22-24 Oct 2024) Oct highlights: (1) 'Kazan Declaration' + 'partner country' category introduced (expansion BRICS+). (2) India-China LAC disengagement just prior (Modi-Xi bilateral first since 2019 Doklam-Galwan). (3) India pushed for BRICS payment system — reducing USD dependence; de-dollarisation discussion. Currency talk (own currency, commodity-backed) rejected by India though not formally. (4) Russia highlighted strategic autonomy + criticism of Western sanctions. CURRENT BRICS+ RANKINGS: (a) China — world's 2nd economy by nominal GDP. (b) India — 5th. (c) Russia — 11th. (d) Brazil — 9th. (e) S Africa — 35th. Among new: Saudi Arabia 17th, UAE 33rd, Egypt 35th, Iran 38th, Ethiopia 50s. QUAD — parallel grouping with DIFFERENT member composition: USA + Japan + India + Australia. Strategic security focus against China's Indo-Pacific footprint. I2U2: India + Israel + UAE + USA (2022 'West Asia Quad'). Other EMERGING — G77 (developing countries, ~134); NAM (non-aligned); IBSA (India-Brazil-S Africa 2003); SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation — China-led, 9 members including India + Pakistan). original 5 + EGYPT + ETHIOPIA + IRAN + UAE + Saudi Arabia (joining officially but status pending); Argentina declined under Milei.

questions.explanation: QUAD / QUADRILATERAL SECURITY DIALOGUE — strategic partnership of 4 countries: USA + JAPAN + AUSTRALIA + INDIA. 'Indo-Pacific Quad'. Focus: democratic values, maritime security, counter-balancing China's rise. ORIGINS: (1) 2004 Indian Ocean TSUNAMI response — coordinated humanitarian response by these 4 countries (with later addition of Indonesia, Singapore, N Zealand). (2) FORMALISED 2007 — Japan's PM SHINZO ABE proposed 'Confluence of 2 Oceans' speech in Indian Parliament (Aug 2007 — spoke of Indo-Pacific connectedness); QUAD DIALOGUE begun 2007 with all 4 + naval MALABAR 2007 exercise (Bay of Bengal). (3) WITHERED 2007-17 — Australia withdrew under Rudd (Labor, pro-China); India under UPA-II cautious. (4) REVIVED 2017 Manila ASEAN sidelines — Trump + Abe + Modi + Turnbull resurrected dialogue. (5) 2020 onwards — intensified; elevated to LEADERS level. 6 QUAD LEADERS' SUMMITS: (1) March 2021 virtual (inaugural; Biden + Suga + Morrison + Modi). (2) Sep 2021 in-person Washington. (3) May 2022 Tokyo (Kishida). (4) Mar 2023 virtual. (5) May 2023 Hiroshima sideline (with G7). (6) Sep 2024 WILMINGTON, DELAWARE (Biden's home; hosted after Quad summit in India was delayed). Planned 2025 India summit. KEY INITIATIVES: (1) QUAD VACCINE PARTNERSHIP — initially pandemic response; India produces (Bharat Biotech Covaxin + SII Covishield); US + Japan funding; Australia logistics. Delivered 600M+ vaccine doses Indo-Pacific. (2) Quad INFRASTRUCTURE PARTNERSHIP — counter to China BRI. (3) Quad CLIMATE Working Group. (4) Quad TECH (critical + emerging tech; 5G, AI, semiconductors; export controls). (5) Quad CYBER + SPACE. (6) IPMDA (Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness) — monitor illegal fishing + vessels. (7) Quad QUAD FELLOWSHIP — 100 students/year in STEM. (8) MALABAR NAVAL EXERCISE — originally India-US (1992); expanded to India-US-Japan (2015); then Australia rejoined (2020 onwards, at India's invitation) — so QUAD navies now drill together regularly. WHY IT MATTERS: (a) RESPONSE to CHINA's expansion — South China Sea, Taiwan pressure, BRI, island-chain buildup. (b) FREEDOM of NAVIGATION + overflight in Indo-Pacific. (c) Democratic values alliance. (d) SUPPLY CHAIN diversification post-COVID. (e) Tech standards vs China-dominated tech norms. CHINA opposes QUAD vehemently — calls it 'Asian NATO' + 'Cold War mentality'. INDIA IS CAREFUL not to label Quad anti-China officially; prefers 'for' free Indo-Pacific rather than 'against' China; maintains STRATEGIC AUTONOMY + nonaligned tradition; participates in both QUAD + BRICS + SCO — unique multi-alignment. Critics say Quad is 'MILITARY-LIGHT' (not a formal alliance; no mutual defence clause); supporters say this flexibility is its STRENGTH. AUKUS (Australia + UK + US, 2021) — separate trilateral SECURITY PACT; AUSTRALIA to get NUCLEAR SUBMARINES via US + UK tech transfer. France furious over cancelled Australian contract. Some see AUKUS as Quad+. RELATED groupings: (1) I2U2 (India + Israel + UAE + USA, 2022) — 'West Asian Quad'. (2) 'CHIP 4' (USA, Japan, S Korea, Taiwan) — semiconductors. (3) G7 + IPEF (Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, 2022) — 14 economies including India. (4) ASEAN + Plus grouping (ASEAN + China, Japan, Korea = APT). NATO — USA-led 32-member military alliance (original 1949 + expansions; Finland 2023, Sweden 2024 latest; Ukraine's bid aggravated Russia invasion). NATO's 'INDO-PACIFIC PARTNERS' = Japan, S Korea, Australia, NZ — increasing engagement. RUSSIA-NATO standoff = backbone of Ukraine conflict. Indo-Pacific strategic alignment; revived 2017; Leaders' summits since 2021; focus on China's rise.

questions.stem: The NON-ALIGNED MOVEMENT (NAM) was founded in:
questions.explanation: NAM (NON-ALIGNED MOVEMENT) — forum of developing countries NOT FORMALLY ALIGNED with any major power bloc during COLD WAR. FOUNDED 1961 at 1ST SUMMIT in BELGRADE (Yugoslavia, 1-6 Sept 1961) with 25 founding members. KEY FOUNDERS — '5 Fathers of NAM': (1) JAWAHARLAL NEHRU — India; PM; chief architect; 5 Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel 1954) + Bandung Spirit. (2) JOSIP BROZ TITO — Yugoslavia; independent socialist; defied Stalin. (3) GAMAL ABDEL NASSER — Egypt; pan-Arabism; Suez nationalised 1956. (4) SUKARNO — Indonesia; hosted 1955 Bandung Asian-African Conference. (5) KWAME NKRUMAH — Ghana; pan-African; Africa's 1st president post-independence. PREDECESSOR event: BANDUNG CONFERENCE (18-24 April 1955, Indonesia) — 29 Asian + African newly-independent states met; 'Dasasila Bandung' (10 principles); seeded NAM movement. KEY PRINCIPLES of NAM (from Belgrade): (1) Mutual RESPECT for territorial integrity + sovereignty. (2) MUTUAL NON-AGGRESSION. (3) Non-interference in internal affairs. (4) EQUALITY + MUTUAL BENEFIT. (5) PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE. (6) NEUTRALITY between USSR + USA. MEMBERSHIP CRITERIA: (1) Policy of independence based on peaceful coexistence + non-alignment. (2) Consistently supporting national independence movements. (3) Not member of multilateral MILITARY ALLIANCE tied to great-power conflicts (US-led NATO or Soviet-led Warsaw). (4) Not member of bilateral military pact with great power. CURRENT: 120 MEMBERS (states) + 17 OBSERVERS + 10 observer organisations = LARGEST intergovernmental grouping after UN. Covers 55% of world's population. INDIA is founding member + ACTIVE. SUMMITS held every 3 YEARS. Chair rotates alphabetically. SUMMIT HISTORY: (1) 1961 Belgrade; (2) 1964 Cairo; (3) 1970 Lusaka Zambia; (4) 1973 Algiers; (5) 1976 Colombo; (6) 1979 HAVANA; (7) 1983 DELHI (Indira Gandhi chaired after coup against Bishop in Grenada); (8) 1986 Harare; (9) 1989 Belgrade; (10) 1992 Jakarta; (11) 1995 Cartagena; (12) 1998 Durban; (13) 2003 Kuala Lumpur; (14) 2006 Havana; (15) 2009 Sharm el-Sheikh; (16) 2012 Tehran; (17) 2016 Isla de Margarita Venezuela; (18) 2019 Baku; (19) 2024 KAMPALA Uganda. INDIA (under Modi) HAS SKIPPED 4 recent NAM summits (2016, 2019, 2024 — sent Vice President; 2016 was 1st ever Indian PM to miss). CRITIQUES: (a) Cold War ended 1991 — what's NAM's relevance? (b) 'NON-alignment' replaced by 'MULTI-alignment' in India's strategic language (S Jaishankar). (c) Internal contradictions — mixed regimes, conflicting interests (e.g., India vs China both joined; Pakistan member; Iran-Saudi-Iraq-Israel; Cuba-USA). (d) Forum of discussion more than action body. DEFENCE of NAM: (a) Represents developing world / Global South collective voice. (b) UN reform push. (c) South-South cooperation. (d) Anti-sanctions (Cuba, Iran, Venezuela). (e) Climate justice + SDGs + debt reform. INDIA's EVOLVING POSITION: (a) Nehruvian non-alignment ideology. (b) Post-1991 economic reforms + rapprochement with USA. (c) Post-2014 Modi + Jaishankar doctrine: 'INDIA will engage with all, align with none' — effectively 'strategic autonomy' + 'multi-alignment' (BRICS + Quad + SCO + G20 + BIMSTEC + NAM + bilaterals all active). (d) De-prioritisation of NAM optics without formal exit. by NEHRU (India) + TITO (Yugoslavia) + NASSER (Egypt) + SUKARNO (Indonesia) + NKRUMAH (Ghana); 120 current members.

questions.stem: The ASEAN (Association of South-East Asian Nations) has how many member states?
questions.explanation: ASEAN (ASSOCIATION of SOUTH-EAST ASIAN NATIONS) — major regional organisation of SE Asian countries. FOUNDED 8 August 1967 via BANGKOK DECLARATION signed by 5 FOUNDING MEMBERS: INDONESIA + MALAYSIA + PHILIPPINES + SINGAPORE + THAILAND. Subsequent expansions: BRUNEI (1984, after independence from UK), VIETNAM (1995, post normalisation), LAOS + MYANMAR (1997), CAMBODIA (1999). Now 10 MEMBERS. TIMOR-LESTE (East Timor) — 11th — admitted 'in principle' 2022, full member targeted by 2025 (observer now). HQ: JAKARTA (Indonesia). TOTAL POP: ~700 million (~8% world). Combined GDP ~$3.6 trillion (5th largest economy bloc). CHARTER adopted 2007 (ratified 2008). OBJECTIVES: (1) Economic growth + social progress + cultural development. (2) Peace + security. (3) Collaboration + mutual assistance. (4) Multi-lateral Cooperation. (5) Respect sovereignty + non-interference + peaceful dispute resolution. ASEAN WAY — consensus-based + non-interference + quiet diplomacy; criticised for softness on Myanmar junta + human rights issues. ASEAN SUMMITS: ANNUAL — 2 meetings per year (ASEAN Summit in November + ASEAN Regional Forum ARF in July; also ASEAN+3, East Asia Summit EAS, RCEP). CHAIRMANSHIP ROTATES alphabetically. 2024 — LAOS; 2025 — MALAYSIA; 2026 — PHILIPPINES. IMPORTANCE of ASEAN: (a) High growth + integration model for developing regions; (b) CENTRAL role in Indo-Pacific architecture — most frameworks 'ASEAN-centric' (Quad + EAS + RCEP); (c) Largest trading partner of CHINA + 3rd partner of USA + INDIA; (d) ASEAN-INDIA FTA (2009 signed, 2010 in force); (e) Major recipient of FDI. KEY MECHANISMS: (1) AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area, 1992). (2) ASEAN ECONOMIC COMMUNITY (AEC, 2015) — single market + production base. (3) RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) — world's LARGEST trade deal; 15 members (ASEAN 10 + China + Japan + S Korea + Australia + NZ); signed 2020, in force Jan 2022. India WITHDREW 2019 (Modi govt) citing deficit concerns + China dominance + agri concerns. (4) ASEAN+1, +3 (with China, Japan, S Korea), +6. (5) East Asia Summit (EAS, 2005, 18 members including India + USA). (6) ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF, 1994) — 27 members incl USA, China, EU. (7) ASEAN Defence Ministers Meeting Plus (ADMM+). (8) ACT EAST POLICY — India's engagement (from Look East Policy 1991 Narasimha Rao, renamed 2014 by Modi); annual summits with ASEAN since 2002; CEPA agreements; infrastructure (Kaladan multi-modal Myanmar-Mizoram transit, India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway). ASEAN CHALLENGES: (1) SOUTH CHINA SEA disputes — China's 'Nine-Dash Line' claim vs Vietnam, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, Taiwan. UNCLOS arbitration 2016 favoured Philippines; China rejected. Artificial islands militarised. (2) MYANMAR coup Feb 2021 — ASEAN's '5-Point Consensus' ineffective; junta atrocities continue. (3) Mekong River water stresses (Chinese upstream dams). (4) Climate change (IPCC most-vulnerable region). INDIA's ACT EAST: (a) Strategic — maritime security, Quad synergy. (b) Economic — RCEP withdrawal setback but bilateral + mini-lateral engagement (India-ASEAN, I-Japan, I-Vietnam, I-Indonesia). (c) Cultural — Ramayana routes, Buddhism diplomacy. (d) North East connectivity — Myanmar, Thailand. INDIA aims at Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI 2019) + SAGAR (Security + Growth for All in the Region, 2015 Maritime doctrine). Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand (1967 founders) + Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia (later); TIMOR-LESTE 11th pending 2025.

questions.stem: The WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION (WTO) was established in:
questions.explanation: WTO (WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION) — only GLOBAL international ORG dealing with RULES of trade between nations. ESTABLISHED 1 JANUARY 1995 (Marrakesh Agreement 1994). HQ: GENEVA, Switzerland. 164 MEMBER STATES (as of 2024) + 22 observers. INDIA is FOUNDING member. PREDECESSOR: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs + Trade) — 1947-1994; provisional body signed by 23 countries after UN failure to form International Trade Organization (US Senate rejected ITO Charter 1950). GATT held 8 'ROUNDS' of trade negotiations; successive tariff cuts. URUGUAY ROUND (1986-94) culminated in WTO's creation + broadened scope (services, IP, investment, agriculture, textiles). FUNCTIONS of WTO: (1) Administer TRADE AGREEMENTS. (2) FORUM for trade negotiations. (3) Settle TRADE DISPUTES (DSB — Dispute Settlement Body; WTO's 'crown jewel' though stressed since 2019 by US blocking AB appointments). (4) MONITOR national trade policies (via Trade Policy Review). (5) TECHNICAL assistance + training for developing countries. (6) COOPERATE with IMF + World Bank. STRUCTURE: (a) MINISTERIAL CONFERENCE (MC) — highest body; meets every 2 years. MC-1 Singapore 1996; MC-13 Abu Dhabi Feb-Mar 2024 (latest). (b) GENERAL COUNCIL — day-to-day; meets in Geneva. (c) COUNCILS for GOODS (CTG), SERVICES (CTS), TRIPS. (d) DIRECTOR-GENERAL — 4-year term. Current DG: NGOZI OKONJO-IWEALA (Nigeria, since Mar 2021, second term 2025-29 announced Dec 2024) — FIRST WOMAN + FIRST AFRICAN DG. Prior: Ronaldo Azevêdo (Brazil 2013-20). PRINCIPLES of WTO: (1) NON-DISCRIMINATION — (a) MFN (Most Favoured Nation) — treat all WTO members equally; (b) NATIONAL TREATMENT — domestic + foreign products/services treated alike. (2) Freer trade via negotiation. (3) Predictability via bindings + transparency. (4) Promoting fair competition. (5) Encouraging development + economic reform. KEY AGREEMENTS: (1) GATT — goods. (2) GATS — services. (3) TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) — patents + copyrights + trademarks. (4) TRIMS (Trade-Related Investment Measures). (5) ANTI-DUMPING, SUBSIDIES + Countervailing, Safeguards agreements. (6) AGREEMENT ON AGRICULTURE (AOA) — liberalising farm trade. (7) SPS (Sanitary + Phytosanitary Measures). (8) TBT (Technical Barriers to Trade). (9) Textiles Agreement (MFA phased out 2005). NEGOTIATION ROUNDS (WTO era): (a) DOHA ROUND / DOHA DEVELOPMENT AGENDA (launched Nov 2001, Qatar) — focused on developing countries' interests; STALLED since mid-2000s due to N-S disputes (agri subsidies, non-agri market access); effectively stuck. (b) BALI PACKAGE 2013 — trade facilitation. (c) Nairobi Package 2015. (d) Geneva Package 2022. (e) Abu Dhabi MC-13 (Feb-Mar 2024) — renewed moratorium on e-commerce customs duties (key for India + African states); TRIPS fisheries; but NO big breakthroughs. INDIA's CONCERNS at WTO: (1) PSH (Public Stockholding for Food Security) — INDIA's MSP + NFSA considered 'trade-distorting' subsidies under AOA; India has permanent 'peace clause' (Bali) but WANTS lasting solution. (2) Fisheries subsidies — India blocked agreements in 2022 protecting fishermen's livelihoods. (3) Digital trade — wants 'more development-friendly' terms. (4) Agriculture — DIFF between developed + developing 'special + differential treatment' not strong enough. (5) Use WTO DSB selectively — INDIA won key US steel + solar cases. DSB APPELLATE BODY — paralysed since 2019 (Trump blocking member appointments; Biden continued); 'multi-party interim appeal arrangement' (MPIA) alternative with 26 countries; USA still blocks. WTO reform critical for rule-based trade. DOHA Declaration on TRIPS + Public Health (2001) allows COMPULSORY LICENSING of drugs in health emergencies (India pioneered via Bayer Nexavar 2012, Gilead Sovaldi). successor to GATT (1947); HQ Geneva; 164 member states; INDIA founding member; Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala current DG (Nigeria).

questions.stem: The INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND (IMF) + WORLD BANK were established at:
questions.explanation: BRETTON WOODS CONFERENCE (UN Monetary + Financial Conference) — 1-22 JULY 1944 at Mount Washington Hotel, BRETTON WOODS, NEW HAMPSHIRE, USA. 730 delegates from 44 ALLIED nations (still WWII — before Germany's surrender May 1945). Goal: plan POSTWAR GLOBAL economic order. Co-chaired by (1) JOHN MAYNARD KEYNES (UK) — proposed 'International Clearing Union' + bancor supranational currency (not adopted); and (2) HARRY DEXTER WHITE (USA) — whose plan largely adopted. RESULTS: (1) IMF (INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND) — formal establishment Dec 1945; began operations 1 March 1947. HQ: WASHINGTON DC. MANDATE: promote international monetary cooperation; exchange rate stability; BoP financing for members in crisis. 191 member states. (2) IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction + Development) — 'ORIGINAL World Bank'; began 1946. For Europe's post-WWII reconstruction + developing countries. Expanded to become WORLD BANK GROUP. (3) BRETTON WOODS SYSTEM of FIXED EXCHANGE RATES — currencies pegged to US DOLLAR, which was pegged to GOLD at $35/oz. Central banks could exchange USD for gold. Ended 15 Aug 1971 when Nixon 'CLOSED THE GOLD WINDOW' (Nixon Shock) due to dollar overhang. Since 1973 — mostly floating exchange rates. IMF STRUCTURE: (1) Board of Governors — ministers of finance / central bank governors from each member. (2) EXECUTIVE BOARD — 24 members, daily operations; US + UK + Japan + Germany + France + China each have own director; others grouped. (3) MANAGING DIRECTOR — 5-year term; by CONVENTION from EUROPE (while WB president from USA — 'gentlemen's agreement'). Current: KRISTALINA GEORGIEVA (Bulgaria, since Oct 2019, 2nd term from 2024). Past: Christine Lagarde (France 2011-19, now ECB Chief), Dominique Strauss-Kahn (France 2007-11). (4) Chief Economist — currently Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas (France). Past: Raghuram Rajan (India, 2003-06 — youngest ever; later RBI Governor 2013-16); Gita Gopinath (Indian-American 2019-22, first woman + first Indian). Indira Gandhi's 1966 devaluation was IMF-mandated. QUOTAS + VOTING: members' contributions (based on GDP + economic openness) determine votes. USA ~17% votes = de facto VETO (since major decisions need 85%). CHINA recently rose to 3rd largest quota share. India is 8th; 2019 reforms slightly increased developing countries' weights. SPECIAL DRAWING RIGHTS (SDR) — IMF's RESERVE ASSET since 1969. Basket of 5 currencies (USD + EUR + JPY + GBP + RMB added 2016). Issued occasionally (largest $650 BILLION in Aug 2021 to fight COVID). Members can exchange SDRs for hard currency. FUNCTIONS: (a) SURVEILLANCE — Article IV consultations (annual assessment of each country). (b) LENDING — BoP crises; conditional loans (controversial); 'Stand-By Arrangements', Extended Fund Facility. (c) Technical Assistance. KEY IMF CRISIS INTERVENTIONS: (1) 1970s-80s LATIN AMERICA debt crisis; (2) 1990s ASIAN Financial Crisis (IMF austerity controversial; 'IMF riots'); (3) 1991 INDIA BoP crisis — IMF + WB loans + conditionality catalysed LPG REFORMS (Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh). (4) 1997 Korea, Thailand, Indonesia; (5) 2001 Argentina; (6) 2008 GREECE Eurozone crisis; (7) 2010-18 BAILOUTS in Europe. (8) SRI LANKA 2022 default — IMF $3B package 2023-24. (9) PAKISTAN recurrent packages. (10) COVID-19 response — massive support to ~90 countries. WORLD BANK GROUP: (1) IBRD (1944/46) — middle-income + creditworthy low-income. (2) IDA (International Development Association, 1960) — poorest countries; interest-free loans + grants. (3) IFC (Int Financial Corp, 1956) — private sector. (4) MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, 1988) — political risk insurance. (5) ICSID (1965) — investment disputes settlement. Current WB PRESIDENT: AJAY BANGA (Indian-American, since June 2023) — first Indian-origin + first person of color to head WB. attended by 44 nations; 'Bretton Woods System' fixed exchange rates tied to gold + USD; collapsed 1971; New Hampshire, USA.

questions.stem: The SHANGHAI COOPERATION ORGANISATION (SCO) has how many full member states (2024)?
questions.explanation: SCO (SHANGHAI COOPERATION ORGANISATION) — Eurasian political + economic + security organisation. FOUNDED 15 JUNE 2001 at SHANGHAI. Evolved from SHANGHAI FIVE (1996) — China + Russia + Kazakhstan + Kyrgyzstan + Tajikistan. Uzbekistan joined 2001 → SCO-6. India + Pakistan 2017 → SCO-8. Iran 2023 → SCO-9. Belarus 9 Jun 2024 → SCO-10. Current 10 members. OBSERVER states: Afghanistan, Mongolia. Dialogue partners: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Cambodia, Egypt, Kuwait, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Turkey, UAE. HQ: BEIJING (secretariat); REGIONAL ANTI-TERRORIST STRUCTURE (RATS) at TASHKENT Uzbekistan. Official languages: RUSSIAN + CHINESE (no English — reflects non-Western orientation). CURRENT SCO CAPACITY: ~40% of global population + ~30% of GDP + ~70% of Eurasian landmass. OBJECTIVES (Shanghai Convention): (1) Strengthen MUTUAL TRUST + neighbourhood + friendship. (2) Encourage COOPERATION in politics, trade, economy, scientific, technology, culture, education, energy, transport + environment. (3) JOINT EFFORTS to maintain peace + security + stability in region. (4) COMBAT 'THREE EVILS' — TERRORISM + SEPARATISM + EXTREMISM. Anti-terror focus pronounced. SCO SUMMITS: ANNUAL Heads-of-State Summit + Heads-of-Government Summit. Chair rotates. Recent: (1) 2022 SAMARKAND Uzbekistan — Iran admitted; Putin attended despite Ukraine war; Modi met Xi first time. (2) 2023 NEW DELHI (India's 1st SCO Summit; held VIRTUAL; India's downgrading amid LAC tensions with China). (3) 2024 ASTANA Kazakhstan — Modi SKIPPED (sent S. Jaishankar); Belarus admitted. (4) 2025 TIANJIN (China). INDIA's SCO dynamics: (1) Joined 2017 (Kazakhstan) along with Pakistan — expected to lead to increased Indo-Pak dialogue; hasn't materialised — 2023 Jaishankar-Bhutto meeting was rare exchange. (2) India's dilemma — SCO is CHINA + RUSSIA dominated; counter-Western; India's strategic autonomy strategy participates but doesn't commit to anti-West rhetoric. (3) RATS cooperation on terrorism useful (intel sharing). (4) Central Asia access — potential for INSTC (International North-South Transport Corridor; India-Iran-Russia route bypassing Pakistan; 15-year stagnation, recent progress with Chabahar port operation 2024). (5) China-India LAC tensions Galwan 2020 cooled enthusiasm. ISSUES: (1) CHINA-INDIA rivalry, LAC border, BRI vs IMEC. (2) India-Pakistan hostility — rare SCO dialogue. (3) Russia's Ukraine war (Feb 2022-) divides members; India abstained at UN votes; doesn't subscribe to 'West'. (4) Iran's admission politicised. (5) AFGHANISTAN situation (Taliban since Aug 2021) — SCO discussions. COMPETITIVE GROUPINGS: (a) NATO (32 members since Sweden 2024). (b) EU (27 members). (c) EAEU (Eurasian Economic Union — Russia + Belarus + Kazakhstan + Armenia + Kyrgyzstan). (d) CSTO (Collective Security Treaty Organisation — 6 members; Russia-led military). (e) QUAD. (f) BRICS+. MULTI-ALIGNMENT is new normal for INDIA: QUAD (USA + Japan + Australia) + SCO (China + Russia) + BRICS (Russia + China + Brazil + S Africa) + G20 + NAM + IBSA + I2U2. S. Jaishankar's doctrine of 'friends of friends, partners of partners'. India's foreign policy = strategic autonomy + issue-based alignment + multi-engagement. original China, Russia + Kazakhstan + Kyrgyzstan + Tajikistan + Uzbekistan; INDIA + PAKISTAN joined 2017; IRAN 2023; BELARUS 2024 (10th).

questions.stem: OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) was founded in:
questions.explanation: OPEC (ORGANIZATION OF THE PETROLEUM EXPORTING COUNTRIES) — cartel of oil-producing nations; controls ~40% of world oil + ~80% proven reserves. FOUNDED 10-14 SEPT 1960 at BAGHDAD CONFERENCE by 5 FOUNDING MEMBERS: IRAN, IRAQ, KUWAIT, SAUDI ARABIA, VENEZUELA. HQ originally GENEVA 1961-65; moved to VIENNA Austria 1965. OBJECTIVES: (1) Coordinate + unify oil policies of members for fair + stable prices. (2) EFFICIENT, economic + regular supply to consumers. (3) Fair return on capital for producers. CURRENT 12 MEMBERS (2024): Algeria, Angola (joined 2007, left Jan 2024), Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Venezuela. Some left over years: Indonesia (suspended 2008, left 2016), Qatar (left 2019), Angola (left 2024). ECUADOR + Indonesia had also joined + left. OPEC+ — in 2016, OPEC formed alliance with 10 non-OPEC producers led by RUSSIA = 23 countries (10 OPEC + 13 non-OPEC). Russia + Kazakhstan + Mexico + Azerbaijan + Oman + Bahrain + Brunei + Malaysia + Sudan + South Sudan. Collectively control ~55-60% of world oil. Meets regularly to set production quotas. DECISIONS + HISTORY: (1) 1973 OIL EMBARGO — OPEC Arab states (OAPEC) banned oil exports to USA + others over Yom Kippur War support of Israel. Oil price quadrupled ($3 → $12/barrel); global recession; US 55 mph speed limit + daylight savings changes; Indian BoP squeeze. Shift of power to oil exporters. (2) 1979-80 — Iranian Revolution + Iran-Iraq War → oil SHOCK-2 ($40/barrel). (3) 1986 — Oil price crash. (4) 1990-91 — Gulf War supply disruption. (5) 2008 — oil hit $147/barrel (all-time high) then crashed in global financial crisis. (6) 2014-16 — SHALE REVOLUTION in USA + oversupply → oil crashed from $110 to $30. (7) 2016 — Saudi + Russia 'OPEC+' deal formalised production cuts. (8) March 2020 — COVID-19 demand collapse; Saudi-Russia price war; oil futures went NEGATIVE (-$37) in April 2020 (first time ever) due to storage lack. (9) 2022 — Ukraine invasion; Russia oil sanctions; G7 price cap $60/barrel on Russian oil (Dec 2022). (10) 2023-24 — OPEC+ cutting production (3-5 M barrels/day) to support prices; Saudi + UAE tensions; Saudi Aramco IPO (largest ever). (11) 2024 — Angola EXITED over quota disputes. (12) OPEC MONTHLY OIL MARKET REPORT (MOMR). SAUDI ARAMCO — world's MOST VALUABLE company sometimes; Crown Prince MBS (Mohammed bin Salman) + Vision 2030 diversification drive (NEOM megacity, entertainment, tourism). WORLD OIL STATS (2024): (1) PRODUCTION — USA #1 (~13 M b/d, shale surged since 2008); Saudi #2 (~10 M); Russia #3 (~9-10 M); Canada 4th; Iraq + UAE + Brazil + Iran. (2) RESERVES — VENEZUELA #1 proven (300B barrels, much heavy), Saudi #2, Iran, Canada (oil sands), Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Russia, Libya, Nigeria. (3) CONSUMPTION — USA #1, China #2, India #3, Japan, Russia, Germany, Brazil. (4) IMPORTS — China #1, Europe, India. Indian dependence ~85% on imports. (5) INDIA's TOP OIL SUPPLIERS: Iraq, Saudi, UAE, Russia (post 2022 discounted), USA, Nigeria. Russia replaced Iraq as top supplier 2023. INDIAN OIL CRISIS CONTEXT: 1991 BoP crisis partly from Gulf War oil spike. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) — Vizag, Mangaluru, Padur; adding more. Future: (1) Renewables replacing oil (EVs, solar); (2) peak oil demand projected 2030; (3) Gulf states diversifying economies; (4) green hydrogen as oil alternative. 5 founders (Iran + Iraq + Kuwait + Saudi Arabia + Venezuela); 12 current members; HQ Vienna since 1965; 1973 oil embargo + 2016 'OPEC+' with Russia.
